column1: # Mandatory fault and lifecycle scenarios (sub-plan 05 Task 2.1; ARCH-09),
# parsed as data by tests/run.sh check-scenarios.
#   needs:   fixture | live | fixture+live: the proof kinds the fault must
#            carry in scenarios.tsv (fixture = a unit or integration case on
#            the dev host; live = a live case on a real target). A fixture
#            proves the mechanism, never the platform (ARCH-09 labels).
#   receipt: <receipt>:<scenario> that carries the live evidence (declared in
#            receipt through its requires rows), or "-" when needs has no live.
# Referenced in scenarios.tsv as fault:<id>. Never drop one silently.

column4: the stack started from stopped answers its first query within the measured bound (live: a stack restart, not a host reboot)
a query after an idle period is answered over re-established connections
after a host sleep the stack answers again without manual repair
while the upstream network is gone the stack fails closed (no direct query), and answers again once it returns, without manual repair
a bridge fetch that cannot reach the distributor keeps the working bridge set
each provider route failing alone never hands its queries to another provider, restarts Tor or repairs the stack
a tor, socat or haproxy child dying unrequested ends the proxy container, so its runtime restarts it whole
a wedged or missing container runtime is bounded and repaired only on evidence
timer passes that fire together act once: one lock winner, no lost or doubled action
missing, malformed or half-written state is refused or recovered, never executed or trusted
a restart that is not acknowledged, refused or answered stale is never taken as done
a packet capture on the target sees no IPv4 or IPv6 DNS packet (port 53 or 853) leave the host during A and AAAA queries and a bridge refresh
bootstrap traffic is an inventoried exception that never carries client queries; the capture names each off-host flow it saw
